(hint): Good morning, Baraka. = Habari za asubuhi, Baraka?
My name is Amani. = Jina langu ni Amani.
I am Emma. = Mimi ni Emma.
I live in Mombasa. = Ninaishi Mombasa.
I come from Arusha. = Ninatoka Arusha.
Nice to meet you, Juma. = Nimefurahi kukuona, Juma.
This is my mother. = Huyu ni mama yangu.
My father is a teacher. = Baba yangu ni mwalimu.
Brother and sister. = Kaka na dada.
Grandmother and grandfather. = Bibi na babu.
This is my friend. = Huyu ni rafiki wangu.
My grandchild is a student. = Mjukuu wangu ni mwanafunzi.
I have a brother. = Nina kaka.
I don’t have a sister. = Sina dada.
Do you have children? = Una watoto?
I have three children. = Nina watoto watatu.
Neema has a friend. = Neema ana rafiki.
My family is lovely. = Familia yangu ni nzuri.
An elder and a young person. = Mzee na kijana.
Tea with milk. = Chai na maziwa.
Coffee with sugar. = Kahawa na sukari.
Rice and beans. = Wali na maharage.
The food is very tasty! = Chakula ni kitamu sana!
Chapati and tea. = Chapati na chai.
How much is the mango? = Embe ni bei gani?
Lower the price, please. = Punguza bei, tafadhali.
Give me five bananas. = Nipe ndizi tano.
I drink tea at the market. = Ninakunywa chai sokoni.
Twelve shillings. = Shilingi kumi na mbili.
What time is it now? = Ni saa ngapi sasa?
Half past nine. = Saa tatu na nusu.
Eight at night. = Saa mbili usiku.
Today and tomorrow. = Leo na kesho.
A week is seven days. = Wiki ni siku saba.
Where is the bank? = Benki iko wapi?
The shop is here. = Duka iko hapa.
The mosque is over there. = Msikiti iko pale.
It’s near the bank. = Iko karibu na benki.
Is it very far? = Ni mbali sana?
Stop here, please. = Simama hapa, tafadhali.
I am going to town by minibus. = Ninaenda mjini kwa matatu.
How much is the fare? = Nauli ni bei gani?
A motorbike taxi is quick. = Boda boda ni haraka.
My house is small. = Nyumba yangu ni ndogo.
Your house is big! = Nyumba yako ni kubwa!
There are three rooms. = Kuna vyumba vitatu.
There is a bed in the room. = Kuna kitanda chumbani.
Four chairs and a table. = Viti vinne na meza.
The tea is on the table. = Chai iko juu ya meza.
It’s under the bed. = Iko chini ya kitanda.
The child is outside. = Mtoto yuko nje.
Today is Monday. = Leo ni Jumatatu.
Tomorrow is Tuesday. = Kesho ni Jumanne.
Saturday and Sunday. = Jumamosi na Jumapili.
I have a stomach ache. = Ninaumwa na tumbo.
My leg hurts. = Mguu wangu unauma.
Mouth and eyes. = Mdomo na macho.
Hand and foot. = Mkono na mguu.
Where is the doctor? = Daktari yuko wapi?
I want medicine, please. = Nataka dawa, tafadhali.
I’ve recovered, thank you. = Nimepona, asante.
Get well soon, my friend. = Ugua pole, rafiki yangu.
The cup is clean. = Kikombe ni safi.
The food is very good! = Chakula ni kizuri sana!
Put the cup on the table. = Weka kikombe juu ya meza.
Open the window, please. = Fungua dirisha, tafadhali.
Every month I go to Mombasa. = Kila mwezi ninaenda Mombasa.
The long rains come every year. = Masika yanakuja kila mwaka.
I don’t have money today. = Sina pesa leo.
The salary is small. = Mshahara ni mdogo.
I’m on holiday tomorrow! = Nina likizo kesho!
I have three books. = Nina vitabu vitatu.
The classroom is big. = Darasa ni kubwa.
What do you like? = Unapenda nini?
Do you have children? = Je, una watoto?
Is it true? = Je, ni kweli?
Three tomatoes and one onion. = Nyanya tatu na kitunguu kimoja.
The chilli is hot! = Pilipili ni kali!
Today we’re cooking pilau. = Leo tunapika pilau.
The stew is very tasty! = Mchuzi ni mtamu sana!
I live in the village. = Ninaishi kijijini.
I will farm Grandma’s field for her. = Nitamlimia bibi shamba.
I’m cooking ugali for you. = Ninakupikia ugali.
Bring me water, please. = Niletee maji, tafadhali.
My neighbour is a farmer. = Jirani yangu ni mkulima.
